messages:
simon: Heads-up — after today's runtime merge (commit 3f8a9d2) we're seeing a p95 decode regression on medium-length inputs (~120-250 tokens). Canary and CI both show the bump. Profiling points at an attention-kernel fallback plus extra memcpy around KV prefetch.

maria: saw the alert. can you paste the CI numbers? is this blocking rollout?

simon: CI perf job shows baseline p95=52ms -> current p95=78ms. Canary hold was triggered automatically. perf-bot posted failing run: job/ci-perf/2026-03-20/42 (link). This is blocking the rollout.

perf-bot: automated: regression detected in ci-perf/42: p95 +50%. failing test: decode_shortseq_mediumbatch.

aj: suspect the fused-op scheduler change that reorders prefetch is the culprit — kernel selector now prefers attn-transpose fallback for medium seqs. quick repro: revert 3f8a9d2 locally and run perf suite.

lucy: can we collect a full perf trace from a canary instance? run these to generate a flamegraph:

```
# on canary node
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

simon: attaching abbreviated flame excerpt from the failing run (top stacks only):

````
runtime::decode
  runtime::kv_prefetch
    memcpy
    attention::transpose_fallback
````

lucy: also pull kernel selection logs + KV stats:

```
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/debug/kv_stats > kv_stats.json
jq . < kv_stats.json
cat /var/log/runtime/kernel_select.log | tail -n 200
```

maria: @aj can you start a bisect? if that commit is first bad we should revert to lift canary hold.

aj: starting bisect now. sequence I'm running:

```
git checkout main
git bisect start HEAD~10 HEAD
git bisect run perf/regression_test.sh
```

simon: quick note from the perf report: memcpy share increased from ~23% -> ~41% around the KV prefetch NVTX ranges, which matches extra copies introduced by the scheduler path.

devops-bot: canary cluster: 3 of 4 nodes still at hold. rollback toggle available in Console > Deploys > Canary (ops).

lucy: I have a small guarded patch that disables the prefetch reorder for medium seqs and keeps the fused scheduler change for long/short edges. running it against CI now. if green I'll open a patch that is effectively a targeted revert.

maria: please tag release manager and update the canary dashboard when you have a PR. we want visibility if we revert.

aj: bisect result: 3f8a9d2 is the first bad commit. creating revert PR now (PR: rwd/revert-3f8a9d2).

simon: ok landing a revert to unblock rollout, then follow-up to reintroduce scheduler improvements behind a stricter heuristic. thanks all :tada:
